title.narrative: Landscapes Côte d'Ivoire

description.narrative: The focus of IDH in Côte d’Ivoire is on developing a balance between forest, agriculture and people. By doing so, IDH supports the implementation of public and private sector commitments towards zero net deforestation and green growth on the ground. IDH aims to address policy opportunities at national level and to develop practical and scalable solutions at local and regional level.

title.narrative: Improved Sector Governance

description.narrative: Change in sector agencies and sector institutions to manage the sector in a sustainable way at local and international levels. Improving sector governance for an enhanced enabling (policy) environment can be considered a pre-condition for changes in business practices to happen

title.narrative: Number of multi-stakeholder coalitions, committees, secretariats, initiatives, and platforms convened to sign and support a common vision, goals, or strategy on sustainable development or sourcing

description.narrative: A multi-stakeholder coalition is a partnership of various stakeholders from the private sector, public sector, civil society, and/or worker/producer representatives or organizations representing the main interests of different stakeholder groups in defined sector, landscape or compact area. This coalition is often referred to as a “platform” or “partnership”. They are mainly convened and work at sector, landscape or compact scales. Multi-stakeholder platforms at the market level are convened at the national (India, China) or multinational level (EU).

title.narrative: Diagnostic analyses finalized

description.narrative: The number of data driven approaches, diagnostic or assessments performed by IDH. This might include diagnostic assessments, data driven approaches, “gap analysis”, Service Delivery Model (SDM) analysis, working conditions, Salary Matrix, or any types of evidence-based consultancy services given by IDH programs to private sector partners to co-develop business cases or assess performances on social, environmental and financial outcomes. An analysis is considered finalized when the report has been published online or privately distributed between companies and IDH.

title.narrative: Number of Value Chain Actors with MoUs, funding agreement to invest, trade, and/or provide services

description.narrative: This indicators measures the unique number of companies with signed funding agreements, MoUs or Letters of Assignment can only be counted once for the year in which these companies joined a contractual partnership with IDH.

title.narrative: Number of multi-stakeholder agreements signed as a result of IDH interventions

description.narrative: Number of multi-stakeholder agreements signed as a result of IDH interventions. A multi-stakeholder agreement is a collection of institutional arrangements, decision-making processes, policy instruments, and underlying values in the system by which multiple actors pursue their interests in sustainable food and manufacturing, ecosystem service conservation, and livelihood security. These institutional arrangements include multi-stakeholder platforms and coalitions that represent the main actors in the sector and landscapes responsible for sustainable production, landscape governance and planning.Typical activities through which IDH seeks to influence sector or landscape governance including supporting the development of policy frameworks – such as Green Growth Plans and Sector Initiatives – including the convening of the multi-stakeholder platforms and coalitions required for these; influencing policy changes or supporting improved enforcement; attracting and mobilizing investments for sustainability solutions; and capacity building of local government.

title.narrative: Number of new or improved policies or standards that are effectively enforced

description.narrative: The total number of new policies (including laws and regulations) launched by governments to enhance sustainable development related to IDH programs + the total number of improved policies (including laws and regulations) that were amended to enhance sustainable development related to IDH programs + total number of voluntary standards that were either created or amended to enhance sustainable business practices in IDH sectors.

title.narrative: Improved Business Practices

description.narrative: Change of behavior of business actors in the value chain, towards more sustainable business practices that contribute to a living wage for workers, living income for farmers, a better environment and gender equalit

title.narrative: Value Chain Actors with improved access to financial services

description.narrative: Number of value chain actors that have access to blended finance, investment deals, commercial loans, lower interest rates, sharing of financing risks, access to funds beyond the borrowing limit, reduced loan tenor terms, or finance that links value chain partners to reduce price risk.

title.narrative: Number of Value Chain Actors that adopted or updated their sourcing, procurement policies or strategies to include sound social and environmental sustainability criteria and goals

description.narrative: The total number of market actors that have adopted new or updated their existing sourcing/procurement policies or strategies to include sound and credible social and environmental sustainability criteria or goals.“Targeted” means that the market actor in question has been identified by the Market’s Program as a priority to help adopt or update their sourcing or procurement policies. “Sound and credible social and environmental sustainability criteria or goals” must be assessed according to existing and operational (international) standards and certification schemes supported by IDH Programs.

title.narrative: Replication of investments and scaling by IDH partners

description.narrative: Models and sustainability solutions with proven business case in the implementation phase are taken to scale and replicated by the private sector companies and markets to truly make a difference.

title.narrative: Other sources of public, private or blended-finance investments/funding leveraged by the program

description.narrative: The total value of all direct and indirect public, private, and blended-finance investments/funding (in euros) committed by (impact) investment funds, donor organizations, and government institutions to support IDH project activities in sustainable commodity production and natural resource protection. These include but not limited to the co-funded projects within IDH program but also result of IDH’s convening work or co-funding of preparatory or capacity building (de-risking) work.Direct funding refers to co-funding contributed by non-private parties in IDH projects. Indirect funding refers to leveraged funding that is not captured in contracts but is a result of IDH’s work.

title.narrative: Proven business cases for field level projects

description.narrative: Sustainability impact at the level of producers, workers and producer communities, including their economic situation, their social well-being, and the sustainability of their natural resource base. For private sector companies to change their business practices it often is a pre-condition that the business case for new ways of organizing production and trade needs to be proven and disseminated.
